formula: as + adj + as (equal) · not as + adj + as (less) · much/far/a bit + comparative · the + superlative + I've ever · the more ..., the better
formula_visual: [as tall as] // [much better than] // [the best film I've ever seen]
when_to_use: To compare precisely: 'as ... as' for equality, 'not as ... as' for less, modifiers (much, far, slightly, a bit) to show the SIZE of a difference, 'the + superlative + I've ever ...' for lifetime records, and 'the more ..., the more ...' for parallel change.
when_to_use_ar: للمقارنة الدقيقة: 'as ... as' للتساوي، 'not as ... as' للأقل، ومعدّلات (much, far, a bit) لحجم الفرق، و'the + التفضيل + I've ever' للأفضل في العمر، و'the more..., the more...' للتغيّر المتوازي.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic uses أفعل من for all comparisons, so learners drop the second 'as' ('as tall than'), use 'more' with short adjectives ('more cheap'), say 'very better' instead of 'much better', and forget 'the' before superlatives.

examples.en: He is as tall as his brother.
This phone isn't as expensive as that one.
My new job is much better than my old one.
examples.ar: وظيفتي الجديدة أفضل بكثير من القديمة

examples.en: It's the best film I've ever seen.
examples.ar: إنه أفضل فيلم رأيته في حياتي

examples.en: The more you practise, the better you get.

common_errors.wrong: He is as tall than his brother.
common_errors.correct: He is as tall as his brother.
common_errors.explanation: Equality uses as ... as; 'than' belongs with comparatives.

common_errors.wrong: It's best film I've ever seen.
common_errors.correct: It's the best film I've ever seen.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: This car is ___ (much) faster than mine.
That was ___ (good) meal I've ever eaten.
___ more you read, ___ more you learn.

quick_rule: Equal → as ... as. Bigger gap → much/far + comparative + than. Record → the + superlative + I've ever. Parallel → the more ..., the more ...
quick_rule_ar: تساوي → as...as. فرق كبير → much/far + المقارنة + than. رقم قياسي → the + التفضيل + I've ever. تغيّر متوازي → the more..., the more...
mnemonic: as–as for equal, than for different, 'the' for the best, 'much' not 'very'.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 9 you practised weak as...as, weak than, and 'the more the better' rhythm. Say: 'as TALL əz his BROther' and 'MUCH BETter thən MINE' — weak 'as' and 'than', stressed adjectives.
